itemTypes.meal: Lunch or dinner, including working sessions over food

items.title: Opening session
items.subtitle: Framing the week: from COP31 commitments to investment-ready planning
items.summary: Welcome remarks from the co-hosts and co-lead countries, and an introduction to the planning value chain that structures the week — scenarios, to investment signals, to implementation.

items.title: Electrification and the COP commitments: implications for scenarios
items.summary: A high-level panel linking electrification to the COP31 climate commitments, building on the discussions at SB64 in Bonn. What does accelerated electrification mean for equitable climate goals, and how should national scenarios be adjusted to capture it? The session examines the aspects of electrification — including those often overlooked — that need to feature in scenarios and plans to inform feasible policies and reveal what is possible, drawing on both qualitative and quantitative evidence. It traces how international electrification goals translate into national planning and connect with local, municipal and urban planning, including the trade-offs, implementation and permitting involved.

items.title: Hybrid scenario capacity across the value chain
items.summary: Capacity as the central enabler of durable scenario work. The focus is on building sustainable national planning ecosystems — working with universities, research institutions and other national bodies to develop and retain capacity, coordinating with partners, and moving countries from dependency on external support toward hybrid, self-sustaining planning ecosystems. It covers institutional mandates and ownership, skills and retention, modelling-tool selection and institutionalisation, and alignment with policy and budget cycles, so that scenario work survives political cycles and feeds directly into policy and budget decisions.
items.note: Reflects the leading governance cluster of the 2026 Priorities Survey.

items.title: Lunch and poster session
items.summary: An extended lunch with a poster session: participants and partner institutions present scenario tools, country cases and ongoing work for informal discussion. As part of IRENA's commitment to next-generation capacity, five young energy planning researchers from developing countries are invited to display their work.

items.title: Data governance, sharing and quality assurance
items.summary: Data as the foundation of credible, repeatable scenarios. For many planning teams the reality is inconsistent access to data and data-sharing platforms, significant gaps in the available data, and heavy reliance on proprietary datasets. The session covers data availability, stewardship and governance; data sharing and harmonisation across agencies and institutions; quality assurance; and the particular data challenges faced by developing-country planning teams — and explores practical solutions.

days.label: Day 2
days.theme: Scenarios for Security, Adaptation and Implementation

items.title: LTES Network members and partners strategic meeting
items.access: Closed-door — LTES Network members and partners only

items.title: Impact session: Brazil's national energy plan and the LTES Network
items.summary: Brazil presents its national energy plan and reflects on how collaboration through the LTES Network contributed to it — an impact spotlight on translating Network learning and peer exchange into national planning practice.

items.title: Energy security and resilience: planning under geopolitical uncertainty
items.summary: How countries stress-test scenarios against geopolitical volatility and fuel-price shocks, and how the fossil-fuel transition and asset risk are treated in national scenario frameworks. Framed around the energy trilemma, the session asks how alternative plans have been conceived to respond to supply disruptions.

items.title: Lunch session: machine learning and AI in energy planning
items.summary: A working-lunch showcase of applied uses of AI prioritised by the Network — demand and load forecasting, scenario development and sensitivity analysis, and data processing and quality assurance — together with the governance and institutional capacities needed for responsible adoption, building on the SAGES framework.

items.title: Climate risks and adaptation
items.summary: The top scenario-design priority of the 2026 Priorities Survey. How scenarios incorporate climate risks and adaptation — heating and cooling demand, floods, droughts and other physical risks — into national energy planning.

items.title: Transformative scenarios: an interface between novel methods and national planning practices
items.summary: Scenario-based energy planning is a constantly evolving field, incorporating new tools and actors and broadening its scope. Many new methods — deep uncertainty and robust decision-making approaches, agent-based modelling, participatory and open-source modelling — are pioneered in research and gradually diffuse into policy-facing work, bringing communities and civil society into the scenario-building process itself. This session explores those methods in conversation with government planners, to understand how they can be navigated within the social, political and economic realities planners contend with, including resource constraints and perceived political non-viability.

items.title: Day 2 wrap and bridge to Day 3
items.summary: Joint reflections by IRENA and GET.transform.

days.label: Day 3
days.theme: From planning signals to investment, and from plans to delivery

items.title: Opening: from the LTES Forum to investment-ready implementation
What countries are telling us about planning, investment and implementation
items.summary: Cross-regional findings from the GCEP regional dialogues and other regional exchanges, focusing on recurring planning-to-investment messages: grids and flexibility, institutional coordination, project preparation, finance-facing planning signals, data and governance, and the practical partner support countries are asking for.

items.title: Global and European perspectives on the planning-to-investment gap
items.summary: This session compares the key planning-to-investment challenges emerging from the regional dialogues with European experience, identifying common barriers and practical lessons for turning long-term energy plans into implementable investments.
items._sourceNote: Draft programme v0.3 lists 09:30–11:00, which overlaps the preceding keynote (09:15–09:45). Start moved to 09:45 pending confirmation.

items.title: Planning the Transition Away from Fossil Fuels
items.summary: The Transition Away from Fossil Fuels (TAFF) agenda through the lens of investment-ready energy planning: how national planning systems can translate transition-away commitments into credible implementation pathways, and what practical support GCEP can provide to facilitate dialogue between planners, policymakers and financiers on the conditions needed to move from political commitment to investable action. It also reflects on the development and climate nexus.

items.title: Implementation: from plans to delivery
items.summary: The Implementation Lab turns to what happens after a plan is approved — permitting, project preparation, system operation, infrastructure delivery and institutional accountability.
